elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to both parties)
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED"

elements.element: Cap structured as the greater of a fee limb and a fixed floor
elements.evidence: "EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) ... AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS"

elements.element: Fee limb = fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim
elements.evidence: "DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE LIABILITY" — event anchor, not the claim
"IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY HAVE ANY LIABILITY ... FOR ANY INDIRECT, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for breach of confidentiality
elements.evidence: "EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OR SECTION 10" (Section 10 confidentiality per comment)

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for data protection and security obligations
elements.evidence: No reference to data protection or security in the carve-out list: "SECTION 8 OR SECTION 10 ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD"
"ARISING OUT OF A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: Only "SECTION 8 OR SECTION 10" cited; no express IP-infringement carve-out and Section 8 scope not shown

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: No such statement anywhere in the revised clause
Cap is "THE GREATER OF (A) ... AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS", not a cap equal to 12 months' fees (though customer-favourable)

elements.element: Carve-outs for gross negligence and wilful misconduct

reasons: The fee limb anchors to "THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE LIABILITY" rather than the playbook's "12 months preceding the claim"; change the anchor to the claim.
No carve-out for data protection and security obligations was added, so the preferred uncapped list is incomplete.
The clause does not state that Customer's payment obligations (amounts due under the Agreement) are not "damages" subject to the cap; add a short sentence.
No express uncapped carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP; Section 8's scope is not shown to cover mutual IP infringement.

Read literally, the greater-of construct is not the fallback's "cap of 12 months' fees" either, so neither level is fully complete — though the greater-of and the $1,000,000 floor are customer-favourable improvements.
Drafting is otherwise tightly scoped: a single targeted replacement of the cap sentence with no extraneous language and no disturbance to the exclusion or risk-allocation sentences.
